title: term_registry.v1
description: Caller-supplied canonical vocabulary, aliases, forbidden mappings and first-mention rules. Canonical entries and aliases resolve deterministically; incompatible meanings remain distinct.

term.description: One canonical vocabulary entry. `id` is the machine key; `canonical` is the literal string as it appears (or should appear) in an underwrite contract schema or UI surface.

id.description: Slug key, unique across the registry. Referenced by other terms' forbidden_merges and by forbidden_mappings.from/to.

canonical.description: The canonical term exactly as used in contracts (e.g. "not_measured", "Approve", "HITL-only"). Unique across the registry.

meaning.description: The one canonical meaning of this term.

tier.description: Vocabulary tier: core = basic user-facing concepts; contract = state, decision and classification terms; appendix = method names and contract versions.

layer.description: Architectural home. "core" = the underwrite_core package (canonical/seal/chain/boundary/absence/registry/bundle/verify); "cross" = spans multiple layers or sits outside all five (product-philosophy vocabulary, Non-Goal boundary concepts).

aliases.description: Names other repos/papers/tools use for this canonical term.

forbidden_merges.description: ids of other terms in this registry that must never be treated as synonyms of this one.

source.description: Reference identifying the declared source of this vocabulary entry.

next_action.description: The usual next action when this term applies (Backup 1's '다음 행동' column, where the term has one).

term.description: The alias string as actually used elsewhere.

source.description: Where this alias is used (repo:path[:line] or research/spec citation).

note.description: Clarifying note, e.g. why the mapping isn't 1:1, or a false-friend warning.

forbidden_mapping.description: A 'wrong merge' pair: from must never be collapsed onto to. from/to each resolve to a term id or canonical string in this registry.

first_mention_rule.description: A rule for how a term must be introduced on first mention per surface (doc, UI, API) to avoid collision with an external false-friend usage.
